document.title: Afghanistan: Longstanding Tensions Between Taliban Leader Omar and Deputy Leader Rabbani Said To Be On Increase (Islama 09020)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Growing tensions between Omar and Rabbani, particularly over protecting bin Laden: Omar rejects expulsion or extradition while Rabbani wants the matter settled before further isolation. An open break is unlikely. Saudi Arabia denied Mullah Rabbani a visa but granted one to Burhanuddin Rabbani. Excised.

mentions.quote: OMAR IS SAID TO BE IN FAVOR OF HIS PRESENCE IN AFGHANISTAN, WHEREAS RABBANI WOULD LIKE TO HAVE THE MATTER SETTLED.

events.description: Unsubstantiated reports that Rabbani, upset over Omar's handling of bin Ladin, may have been involved in a coup attempt against Omar.
Mullah Rabbani went to Dubai in early December, officially for a medical check-up.
Burhanuddin Rabbani visited Jeddah, performed umrah and met Saudi officials, reportedly including the intelligence chief.
Press reports that Mullah Rabbani applied for a Saudi visa while in the UAE and was denied.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting on Omar-Rabbani tensions.
Burhanuddin Rabbani reportedly visited Saudi Arabia, his first visit in over two years; Saudis used it to signal displeasure with Taliban; reportedly met intelligence chief Prince Turki.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable assessing worsening Omar-Rabbani tensions with no sign of an impending public break.
Mullah Rabbani went to Dubai (UAE) since early December, reportedly for medical check-up or to wait out tensions with Omar.
Unsubstantiated reports that Rabbani was involved in a coup attempt against Omar.
Burhanuddin Rabbani visited Jeddah, performed umrah and met Saudi officials.
Saudi government reportedly denied Mullah Rabbani a visa to visit Saudi Arabia.
Rabbani may have left Dubai for Karachi to meet pro-Taliban Afghans.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable reporting increased Omar-Rabbani tensions.

sources_cited: Confidential sources of the Embassy POLOFF
key_claims: Tensions between Mullah Omar and deputy Mullah Rabbani were reportedly increasing in December 1998.
The dispute centers on bin Ladin: Omar rejects expelling or extraditing him, while Rabbani wants the matter settled to avoid isolation and repair relations with Saudi Arabia.
Rabbani has long rivaled Omar for control of the Taliban and retains the support of many Taliban officials and commanders.
The Taliban and Rabbani publicly attribute his Dubai stay to medical reasons, but sources say this is cover for waiting out the dispute.
Sources doubt a final break, since Omar fears civil war within the movement and Rabbani has many allies.
Saudi Arabia used the visit of anti-Taliban Burhanuddin Rabbani as a signal of its displeasure with the Taliban.
